F-14&20, Uii Building, Connaught Place, New Delhi. .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Date of accident : 08.03.2017 Date of filing of Dar : 27.10.2017 Date of Decision : 13.04.2023 Mact No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act. 2. As per the investigation carried out by concerned police official on 08.03.2017, concerned police Satish Kumar vs Poonam Mittal on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153488709/ 1 officials on call received went to the place of accident and it was informed that injured is already taken in three-wheeler to a unknown hospital by the public. Later on, in Batra hospital, New Delhi, statement of injured/claimant Satish Kumar was recorded. He stated that he is working as conductor in DTC and was going on his motorcycle DL-3SBW-3810 from Badarpur to his home. When he reached under the flyover on Badarpur Mehrauli road at about 3.45 PM, the offending car bearing no. DL-3CCA-0814 Swift Dzire driver came in rash and negligent matter at high speed from behind and hit his motorcycle from behind and caused this accident. He fell down alongwith his motorcycle. The public apprehended the driver of the car alongwith such car. When public was taking the injured in a three wheeler, such lady car driver run away from the spot of the accident but he can identify her. 3. Accordingly, initially FIR u/s 279, 337 IPC was registered. Later on, charge sheet u/s 279, 338, IPC filed against the R-1 apart from filing of present DAR. 4. As per record, R-1/driver-cum- owner appeared and even filed their reply. In the reply filed by R-1, it is claimed that accident is not caused by them and there is no rash and negligent driving on the part of R-1. It is further claimed that it is the claimant/injured himself was driving his motorcycle in zig-zag MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 2 of 26 BK manner and came from behind and in order to overtake the vehicle of R-1, he could not control his vehicle and fell down on the road and received injuries on his body. As such, it is further claimed that accident is caused due to negligence of injured himself. It is further stated that IO has suppressed material facts in the DAR. It is further claimed that injured was under the influence of alcohol at the time of alleged accident and medical record of the injured is suppressed by the IO. 5. Further, reply dated 30.11.2017 filed by insurance company/R-2. In nutshell, it is claimed by R-2 that offending vehicle was insured with such company but it is stated that verification of DL report is not filed and instead a report from MLC is filed that record of DL is not traceable. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal on 05.01.2018: It appears that in issue number 1, it is inadvertently mentioned by my learned predecessor that such vehicle is not insured. Whereas, in fact such vehicle is insured as admitted by R-2 insurance company. Further, no prejudice caused due to such inadvertent mistake to any of the party, accordingly, in issue number 1, it need to be added that such vehicle was insured by MACT No.: Satish Kumar vs Poonam Mittal on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153488709/ 2 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 3 of 26 BK R-2. In fact, R-2 insurance company contested the inquiry throughout. 8. Claimant/petitioner examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary, MLC, educational certificate, salary slip and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/8. He was cross- examined at length by learned counsel for R-1 as well as insurance company/R-2. 9. Further, one Ashok Kumar Khosla, Manager, Sukhdev Vihar, New Delhi was examined as PW-2 to prove the income related documents from DTC. He proved on record Master Attendance register relating to injured as Ex.PW-2/2 (colly) (OSR). Further, salary slip for the month of March, 2017, Ex. PW-2/3(OSR) and verification of date of appointment details of injured Ex. PW-2/4(colly). 10. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 11. In this case, R-1 Poonam Mittal examined herself as R- 1W-1. She filed her examination of chief by way of affidavit Ex. R-1W-1/A. Further, as per record, such witness was cross- examined by learned counsel for claimant as well as by insurance company. 12. Further, even the insurance company examined one Ms. Lalita Anand, Administrative Officer of such insurance company as R-3W-1. She filed her examination in chief by way of affidavit Ex. R-3W-1/A. Such evidence was basically to prove that R-1 was not having valid driving licence at the relevant time. As per record, such witness is not cross-examined by R-1 or claimant despite opportunity given. MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 4 of 26 BK 13. But further, from record, it is noted that insurance company only examined another witness Sh. Ajay Kumar Samal as R-3W-1, from District Transport office, Sarai Kale Khan, Delhi. 14. No other witness was examined by respondent side. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 18. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 19. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1, it is noted that PW-1/Victim/Injured/Petitioner deposed on the lines of petitioner's original stand as already noted above. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place.

In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 5 of 26 BK investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. He further denied the suggestion that the was trying to overtake the car by high speed and in a zig- zag manner. He further denied the suggestion that due to pothole in the road, he fell down from the motorcycle. On the other hand, it is deposed by driver of such alleged offending vehicle, Ms. Poonam Mittal in her examination in chief by way of affidavit, her vehicle is not involved in the accident, she further deposed that it was learnt that injured/claimed was under the influence of alcohol and was illegally driving the vehicle on road. She further deposed that accident was caused by some other vehicle. She further deposed that she was diligently and properly driving the car and did not make any mistake or error. She further admitted that criminal case trial is pending before concerned learned Magistrate. She further admitted that she has not filed any separate complaint to any authority disputing the accident allegedly committed by her. But she denied the suggestion that accident was caused due to her rash and negligent driving. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 30. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 9 of 26 BK medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non -pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 30.1. 30.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 30.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 30.7. It is submitted that as per medical disability certificate , petitioner received 40% disability in right ankle. It is further argued by petitioner side that accordingly functional disability of at least of 40% in relation to whole body be taken in the present case. 41. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel or insurance company that there is no functional disability of 40 % in any case, in the present case. It is further argued that there is no functional disability in the present case at all which is also clear from cross-examination of such witness. 42. Regarding compensation towards future prospect having regard to the ratio of judgment of Rajkumar (Supra) read with facts of present case, it is noted that claimant/injured himself MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 14 of 26 BK deposed that his job is of conductor in DTC bus. Further, during cross-examination, he admitted that he is leading normal life and performing all his work. The MACT No.: 852/17 Satish Kumar v. Poonam Mittal Page No. 15 of 26 BK nature of injuries are grievous and petitioner suffered 40% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right ankle. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. The rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case and taking all relevant factors including inflation, change of economy, policy being adopted by Reserve Bank of India from time to time, how long the case is pending, permanent injuries suffered by the victim, enormity of suffering, loss of future income, loss of enjoyment of life etc. into consideration.
